intended_object: One cached rational interval (an `IntervalRat` with exact rational endpoints) that encloses one Jacobian entry. It is part of a machine-generated LeanCert certificate for the Gerver sofa computation. I inferred this from the docstring ("Exact cached Jacobian interval number 43, shared by equal entries"), from the name, and from where it sits: an auto-generated `KernelOnly/Core/Bundle` file.
explanation: The definition is a constant: two explicit rational endpoints, written with `naturalFromChunks`, plus a proof by kernel `decide` that the lower endpoint is at most the upper one. It is cached certificate data for verified interval arithmetic in the computer-assisted part of the Gerver sofa proof. It is an implementation detail with no mathematical counterpart of its own, so there is nothing to compare against a standard definition. Whether the interval really encloses the intended Jacobian entry is a matter for the theorems that use the certificate, not for this definition.
